L001: Tabs are not allowed in indentation; Tantu indents with spaces only.
L002: An unindent does not line up with any enclosing indentation level.
L003: An illegal character appeared in the source.
L004: An unknown escape sequence appeared inside a string literal.
L005: A string literal was opened but never closed before end of line/file.
L006: A numeric literal is malformed, for example a misplaced underscore like `1_`, `_5`, or `1._5`.
P001: An unexpected token was found where the grammar expected something else.
P002: The source ended in the middle of a construct the parser was still reading.
P003: Expression, type, or pattern nesting is too deep for the parser to read safely.
E0001: This construct is syntactically valid but not supported in the current build.
E0101: A name is defined twice in the same scope.
E0102: Assignment to a `let` binding; declare it `var` if it must change.
E0103: A closure or fiber tried to capture a `var`; copy it into a `let` first.
E0104: The condition of an `if`/`while` is not a `Bool`.
E0105: A `match` does not cover every variant of the scrutinee's type.
E0106: `?` was used on an `Option` inside a `Result`-returning function (or vice versa).
E0107: The element type of an empty list `[]` can't be inferred; add an annotation.
E0108: A function that should return a value ends in a `Unit`-typed statement.
E0109: An intrinsic (like `send`) was used outside call position; it is not a value.
E0111: A referenced name is not defined in any enclosing scope.
E0112: A value's type does not match the type expected here.
E0113: `==`/`!=` used on a type Tantu does not treat as comparable.
E0115: A type annotation names a type that does not exist.
E0118: A call passed the wrong number of arguments.
E0119: A generic call is underdetermined; a type parameter couldn't be inferred.
E0120: A `match` arm can never be reached (a prior arm already covers it).
E0121: A pattern names a constructor that isn't a variant of the matched enum.
E0122: A variant pattern or constructor has the wrong number of fields.
E0123: A bare enum constructor was used as a value instead of being called/matched.
E0124: Two variants of an enum share the same name.
E0130: The module import graph contains a cycle.
E0131: An `import` names a module file that can't be found.
E0132: A qualified access `mod.member` names a member the module doesn't export.
E0133: A module name was used as a value rather than accessed with `.member`.
E0134: `import` was used where there is no source file on disk (stdin/REPL).
E0135: A `select`'s `else` arm must be the single, last arm.
E0136: A generic function was used as a value; it is call-only; wrap it in a lambda.
R001: Division or modulo by zero at runtime.
R002: A list index was out of range at runtime.
R003: A `send` was attempted on a closed channel.
R005: Deadlock: every fiber is blocked and none can make progress.
R006: A global was read before its initializer ran.
R007: A `match` at runtime found no matching arm (should be prevented by the checker).
R008: Execution exceeded the playground's instruction budget (runaway loop safeguard).
R009: A builtin hit a domain error at runtime (for example converting `nan`/`inf` to an integer).
R010: The call stack overflowed; recursion exceeded the frame cap.
R011: A channel was created with a negative capacity.
